inlines.text: Why not copy your cookies into a fresh browser?

blocks.text: Because a fresh automation browser is a different device. You can export cookies and load them, for example with Playwright MCP's --storage-state, which loads cookies and local storage from a file into an isolated browser context (README). It works on some sites and can fail on sites that tie sessions to your device or ask you to sign in again:

blocks.text: 3. Chrome DevTools MCP, auto-connect mode

Google's Chrome DevTools MCP is built around debugging: performance traces, network requests, console messages. By default it starts a new Chrome with a dedicated profile. On Chrome 144 or later, --autoConnect attaches it to the Chrome you already run (advanced usage, Chrome blog).

blocks.text: Safety
An agent in your signed-in browser can do anything you can: send email, change settings, buy things. The vendors say so plainly.

inlines.text: An agent in your signed-in browser can do anything you can: send email, change settings, buy things. The vendors say so plainly.
Prompt injection is the main risk.

Anthropic calls it "the biggest risk facing browser-using AI tools": instructions hidden in a page, email or document can trick the agent into actions you didn't ask for, such as sending your data somewhere. With Claude Opus 4.8 and its current defenses, attack success was under 0.08% in Anthropic's internal testing, and it says the risk is still not zero (
). OpenAI tells you to treat page content as untrusted and not to send secrets through browser tasks unless you have to (
Use a separate Chrome profile when you can.
Anthropic recommends a separate browser profile without access to sensitive accounts such as banking, healthcare and government. With an extension, install it only in that profile; Playwright MCP's

picks which profile it connects to. Tools that attach to the whole browser, like Chrome DevTools MCP and Browser Harness, see what that Chrome has open, so keep the sensitive accounts in a Chrome you don't attach to.
Know what the agent can reach.
Chrome DevTools MCP warns that it exposes the browser's content to your MCP client (
). For the manual setup, where you start Chrome with
, it warns that any application on your machine can connect to that port and control the browser (
). The Chrome 144+ toggle used by auto-connect mode, Gemini CLI's
mode and Browser Harness instead shows a dialog asking you to Allow each connection (
). Either way, turn remote debugging off when you're done.
Review actions on email and payment sites.

Keep approval prompts on for anything that sends, pays or deletes. Claude in Chrome asks before it uses financial sites, the ChatGPT extension asks before each new site, and Gemini CLI asks before every form fill.
